  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Accessible charts}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
options(highcharter.google_fonts = FALSE)
```

Highcharter includes the Highcharts accessibility module in the shared bundle.
Give the chart a title and identify the units on its axes. Use the caption
for the takeaway and the point description for details when navigating the
series. Keep a distinct marker or dash style when several series use color.

```{r accessible-chart}
highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Daily bicycle trips") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed"), title = list(text = "Day")) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Trips")) |>
  hc_add_series(data = c(24, 35, 30), name = "North route") |>
  hc_add_series(data = c(18, 28, 26), name = "South route", dashStyle = "Dash",
                marker = list(symbol = "diamond")) |>
  hc_caption(text = "Both routes had the most trips on Tuesday.") |>
  hc_chart(animation = FALSE) |>
  hc_plotOptions(series = list(animation = FALSE)) |>
  hc_accessibility(enabled = TRUE, landmarkVerbosity = "one",
    point = list(valueDescriptionFormat = "{xDescription}, {value} trips."),
    keyboardNavigation = list(enabled = TRUE)) |>
  hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE, showTable = TRUE)
```

Use Tab to reach the chart, the arrow keys to explore points, and Tab again
to reach the legend and export controls. The HTML data table offers the values
in reading order. Give every interactive chart a visible focus indicator.
For a longer explanation, reference an adjacent paragraph by its unique CSS
selector in `hc_accessibility(linkedDescription = "#route-summary")`.
Use `screenReaderSection` to customize the text before or after the chart.

For Maps, name each region or point and include the unit in its value
description. For Stock, identify the financial instrument and date. See the
[Maps](maps.html) and [Stock](stock.html) examples. The example above disables
introductory animations. The home example respects reduced motion and lets
readers select either measurement. Sonification is available
through `hc_sonification()` for readers who choose to play the chart.

[Highcharts accessibility guide](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/accessibility/accessibility-module)

## Screen readers and sound

Accessibility does not make a chart play sound automatically. A screen reader
speaks its descriptions when you navigate to the chart. Sonification is a
separate, opt-in way of listening to the values as musical notes.

```{r chart-sound}
highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Listen to the weekly pattern") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri")) |>
  hc_add_series(name = "Trips", data = c(24, 35, 30, 42, 38)) |>
  hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE,
    buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = list("playAsSound")))) |>
  hc_sonification(enabled = TRUE, duration = 1800, masterVolume = 0.35)
```

Choose **Play as sound** in the export menu. Playback starts only after that
action; it does not compete with screen-reader speech when the page opens.
